<0>assistant-ui</0> starts from state. You wrap your app in `AssistantRuntimeProvider`, pick a runtime for your backend, and its components read the thread from that runtime. Branching, editing, attachments, tool approvals and resumable streams come from the runtime, and its styled components already show states like a stopped run or a failed reply. That is a lot of work done for you, and the trade is that your chat lives inside its model. Moving off it later means rewriting the state as well as the screens.

assistant-ui is a chat framework: a runtime that manages the conversation, with components that read from it. HextaUI gives you finished screens as plain components, and leaves the state where it already is. This page compares them as of October 2026.
assistant-ui is a free chat framework with its own runtime. HextaUI gives you finished AI screens that read AI SDK message parts and leave the state to you.
